cards.p: A client asks what [service] costs. Reply with my range [range], what changes the price, and two open times.
A spot opened at [time] today. Write a short text for my waitlist. First to reply gets it.
Write 5 questions to text a new color client before the visit: hair history, photos, budget, time.
Write a text and a post with my holiday hours [dates], the last booking day, and how to book early.
Explain kindly why going from [current color] to [goal] takes [X] visits. Plain words, no salon jargon.
A client says their cut feels uneven. Write a calm text inviting them back for a free fix within [days].
Write a short text after a [service]: what to avoid for 48 hours and what to use at home.
Write a warm birthday text for [client] with a small treat: [offer]. Two sentences, no pressure to book.
Give me one natural line to say at the chair, when a client loves the result, asking for a Google review.
This review praises [stylist] by name: [paste]. Write a reply that thanks the client and credits the stylist.
Reply to this review about a long wait: [paste]. Own it, say what changed, under 60 words.
Reply to a review that says we cost too much: [paste]. Thank them, explain what the price covers, stay warm.
Here is a before and after of a [service]. Write 5 captions: story, tip, question, price, booking push.
Write a carousel: 5 cuts for [hair type], one line each on who it suits and how to ask for it.
Write a short intro post for [stylist]: what they love doing, one fun fact, how to book them.
It is a slow [day]. Write a story post with two open times and a reason to book today. No discount.
Sort these salon expenses into products, rent, tools, marketing, other: [paste]. Total each. Flag anything odd.
Write a friendly reminder to [renter] that booth rent of [amount] was due [date]. Add how to pay.
Lay out my service menu with prices: [paste]. Group cuts, color and treatments. Short names, one line each.
Write one honest line to suggest [product] at checkout, tied to the service they just had. Never pushy.
Write a 10 step reset checklist for my station between clients: tools, towels, chair, floor, mirror.
Write a team rule for swapping shifts: how much notice, who approves, how clients get told. Plain words.
Give me 6 interview questions for a [stylist or barber] that show skill, attitude and how they treat clients.
Turn these notes into a 10 minute team huddle: one win, one fix, one goal for the week: [paste].
